notes.meaning: Isaac was now very old and nearly blind. Believing his death might be near, he called his older son Esau to prepare him for a final blessing. This special blessing was meant to pass down God's covenant promises to the next generation.
Isaac knew his body was weakening, even though he did not know the exact day he would die. Because life is uncertain, he wanted to finish his most important family and spiritual duties without delay.
Isaac told Esau to take his hunting gear, including his bow and quiver, and go out into the fields. He wanted his son to hunt wild game and bring it back home for him.

Isaac asked for a flavorful meal of wild game so that he could bless Esau from his heart before dying. Sharing a meal often sealed a sacred family agreement in the ancient world. In his affection for Esau, Isaac overlooked God's earlier revelation that the younger son was chosen to lead.
Rebekah was listening while Isaac spoke to Esau. As soon as Esau went out into the open fields to hunt, she began working on a way to keep the blessing from going to him.
Rebekah reported Isaac's conversation to Jacob. She stressed that Isaac planned to bless Esau in the presence of the Lord, which would make the patriarchal blessing official and binding.

Rebekah told Jacob to listen carefully and obey her exact instructions. She wanted to secure God's promised blessing for Jacob, but she chose human manipulation rather than trusting God to fulfill His word.

Rebekah told Jacob to fetch two young goats from their flock so she could prepare a savory meal just the way Isaac liked it. Jacob was to carry the dish to his blind father so he would receive the blessing instead of his brother.

Jacob pointed out a major problem with the plan, noting that Esau was very hairy while he had smooth skin. At this moment, Jacob seemed more concerned about the risk of being caught than the wrongness of the deceit.
Jacob worried that his blind father would touch him and discover the trick. If that happened, Isaac would see him as a mocker, and Jacob feared bringing a curse on himself instead of a blessing.

Rebekah told Jacob that she would take the blame and any curse upon herself. She was so convinced that God intended the blessing for Jacob that she made a rash promise and insisted that he simply obey.
Jacob gave in to his mother's urging and brought the two young goats to her. Rebekah then cooked the meat into a savory dish that tasted like the game Isaac loved.

Rebekah took Esau's best clothes, which were stored in her tent, and dressed Jacob in them. These garments carried the natural outdoor scent of Esau and helped complete the disguise for the blind patriarch.
Rebekah placed goat skins over Jacob's hands and the smooth part of his neck. The silky hair of these young goats felt similar enough to human hair to fool Isaac's failing sense of touch.
Rebekah handed the freshly cooked meat and bread to Jacob. Jacob was now fully disguised and sent to carry out the deception before his father.
Jacob entered his father's room and announced his arrival. Isaac responded immediately, but his suspicion was stirred right away as he asked which son was speaking.

Jacob directly told his father an outright lie, claiming to be Esau the firstborn. He asked Isaac to sit up and eat the meat so that he could pronounce the blessing. Starting down the path of deception quickly forced Jacob to multiply his falsehoods.

Isaac was surprised that the hunt had ended so quickly and asked how it was possible. Jacob made his deception worse by claiming that the Lord had brought the game to him, using God's holy name to cover a lie.
Isaac remained suspicious of the voice and the quick return, so he asked Jacob to step closer. He wanted to feel his son's body to prove whether he was truly Esau.
Jacob came near and let his father touch him. Isaac was puzzled by the mixed signals, noticing that the voice clearly belonged to Jacob while the hairy hands felt like Esau's.
Isaac did not discover the fraud because Jacob's hands felt hairy like his brother's. Convinced by his sense of touch rather than his hearing, Isaac prepared to bestow the covenant blessing upon him.
